thread:
leo: Heads-up: noticed an archived synthetic payload in vendor-monitor-exports bucket that contains a base64 blob that looks like a KMS-wrapped service account key. object: s3://vendor-monitor-exports/synth/2026-05-10/payload-4821.json

priya: can you paste the snippet (sanitized)?

leo: sanitized snippet: \"metadata\": { \"check_id\": \"ingest-health-7\", \"kms_blob\": \"CiQAQw...base64...==\" }
starts with CiQA which matches our KMS envelope header. vendor said they export raw test payloads to their analysts.

denis: treat as exposed. vendor analysts are external and could have copies. immediate plan: 1) assume SA key compromise for the principal referenced by the blob 2) revoke the SA keys + disable the SA 3) create rotated SA and KMS key, rewrap and push new blob to monitoring config 4) revoke vendor access to the archive bucket and request deletion of the object copies 5) audit KMS decrypt calls and S3 GETs for the object.

sec-bot: @leo flagged object: vendor-monitor-exports/synth/2026-05-10/payload-4821.json -> potential KMS ciphertext exposure. Severity: high.

infra-oncall: agree with denis. I'll snapshot current IAM and S3 ACLs and remove vendor read while we investigate. Priya, can you coordinate vendor takedown and ask them to quarantine/delete exported objects?

priya: pinged vendor-eng and vendor-security. asking for immediate deletion and confirmation. told them not to access or redistribute any payloads that contain `kms_blob`. Also asked them to pause synthetic exports for our org.

leo: I extracted the blob to gs://sec-incident/3265432100/kms_blob.bin for analysis. DO NOT DELETE original S3 object until chain-of-custody completed.

denis: commands I'll run (examples):
```
# IAM snapshot
gcloud iam service-accounts get-iam-policy redwood-monitoring@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com --format=json > /tmp/iam-monitor-snapshot.json
# audit S3 object reads (aws cli example)
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket vendor-monitor-exports --prefix "synth/2026-05-10/" > /tmp/vendor-objects.json
# query access logs (if enabled)
aws s3api get-object --bucket vendor-monitor-exports --key access-logs/2026-05.log /tmp/2026-05.log || true
```

infra-oncall: removed vendor principal vendor-analytics@vendor.iam.gserviceaccount.com from S3 bucket ACL at 09:18 PT and recorded CHG-3265-BUCKET-LOCK. Also disabled vendor's monitor export job on our integration.

priya: vendor confirmed deletion of the specific object and any analyst copies. They will provide an audit of deletions and confirm no downstream copies exist. Asking them to give hashes of deleted objects so we can match.

sec-bot: Incident ticket INC-2026-3265 created and posted to #incidents and #product-security.

leo: key identification: ciphertext header references cryptoKey projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/monitoring/cryptoKeys/mon-sa-key. Running KMS audit for Decrypt in last 30d.

denis: we need to rotate both the service account and the KMS key. Rationale: wrapped private key leaked to external party; even if vendor lacked KMS decrypt perms, better to rotate to reduce blast radius. Plan: create rotated SA redwood-monitoring-rotated, generate new key JSON, create new keyring monitoring-rotate-3265 and a new cryptoKey, wrap rotated key, update monitoring config and vault entries, and roll out with a short maintenance window.

priya: timeline: I can coordinate vendor pause for a 2-hour window this afternoon. prefer to do rotation within next 4 hours. Denis, can you provision rotated artifacts and infra-oncall handle the Vault/KMS/VPC updates?

denis: yes. sample commands I'll run: 
```
# create rotated SA
gcloud iam service-accounts create redwood-monitoring-rotated --project=redwood-prod
# create key for SA
gcloud iam service-accounts keys create /tmp/monitor-rotated.json --iam-account=redwood-monitoring-rotated@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com
# create kms keyring/key
gcloud kms keyrings create monitoring-rotate-3265 --location=global || true
gcloud kms keys create mon-rotate-3265-key --location=global --keyring=monitoring-rotate-3265 --purpose=encryption
# wrap
gcloud kms encrypt --location=global --keyring=monitoring-rotate-3265 --key=mon-rotate-3265-key --plaintext-file=/tmp/monitor-rotated.json --ciphertext-file=/tmp/monitor-rotated.json.enc
# push to vault
vault kv put secret/data/monitoring/sa-key mon_key_enc=@/tmp/monitor-rotated.json.enc
```

infra-oncall: after push we'll run a staged deploy to monitoring staging cluster and verify synthetic checks run successfully. Also will revoke old SA keys and remove KMS IAM bindings on mon-sa-key except for audit retention.

priya: vendor provided deletion confirmation and object hashes at 10:02 PT. They also confirmed they never attempted KMS decrypt and their analysts do not have KMS roles. They've committed to changing export config to redact `kms_blob` fields going forward.

leo: audit results: no Decrypt calls from vendor principals for mon-sa-key in last 90 days. Decrypt calls only from our internal monitoring CA and CI systems. Still rotating as planned.

denis: RBAC change: temporarily remove roles/iam.serviceAccountKeyAdmin from monitoring SA consumer roles and lock iam.serviceAccounts.getAccessToken. I'll push short-lived change and log it: CHG-3265-SA-LOCK.

infra-oncall: smoke test passed on staging at 11:34 PT. Proceeding with production rotate at 12:10 PT in a 30-minute window.

sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-3265 status -> rotation in progress.

priya: rotation complete at 12:23 PT. new SA and KMS-wrapped blob deployed, old SA keys revoked, vendor access removed permanently until they complete onboarding remediation. Vault updated at secret/data/monitoring/sa-key and ACLs tightened.

leo: follow-ups: 1) add a filter in monitoring export to scrub fields named `*_blob` or any base64 starting with CiQ prefix 2) update vendor onboarding checklist to forbid exporting raw wrapped keys 3) add detector job to scan vendor export bucket for KMS header prefixes weekly 4) update runbook to include vendor takedown template.

denis: created follow-up tickets: SEC-3265-SCRUB, DOC-3265-VENDOR-ONBOARD, INFRA-3265-DETECT. Also added a CI preflight check for monitoring config to fail if any `kms_blob` fields are present in synthetic payloads.

sec-bot: Incident INC-2026-3265 status -> resolved (rotation complete, vendor deletion confirmed). Follow-ups queued.

priya: thanks everyone. preserving logs/evidence in gs://sec-incident/3265432100/ for 90 days. Closing thread once vendor audit artifacts are received. :white_check_mark:
